findings.quote: A line never gives the same output twice.
findings.problem: As written, this sentence is false for a horizontal line: y=3 gives the output 3 for every input. The condition 'that is not horizontal' sits only in the sentence before, and this sentence restates the rule as a bare 'never' about every line. The lesson itself later says 'A constant function ($a=0$) is not' one-to-one, so the two sentences contradict each other. A student who takes the sentence at its word and meets y=3 on 1<x<=4 would leave the output 3 out of the range and get an empty range instead of {3}. The round-3 Blocker (falling line) is fixed; this is the same family of unqualified line rule in the same paragraph.
findings.source: reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit (test each 'never' against a known exception); content-checklist B01, L27; the lesson's own Inverse Functions section
